newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-URMANOV WINS SHORT PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-URMANOV WINS SHORT PROGRAMME.

text.p: Olympic and European figure skating champion Alexei Urmanov of Russia edged nearer the only major title he has not won by heading a high quality jumping display in the short programme at the world championships on Wednesday.
The 23-year-old from St Petersburg scored a narrow victory over titleholder Todd Eldredge of the United States, with Russian Ilya Kulik third in an exciting battle of supreme athleticism.
It needed a tie-break to separate the top two for neither had a majority of first place votes from the nine judges.
Urmanov had four, the American three, but in the combined total of first and second place votes, the Russian emerged with seven to Eldredge's four.
Kulik, who had the other two first place votes, had the same number of seconds as Eldredge but lost the runners-up position because he had one less third place than the American.
Yet whichever of those three wins the free skating final on Thursday night will take the gold medal.
"It was a tough start to the competition because there were so many good programmes and it's going to be tough again tomorrow," Urmanov said.
"I'm going to go out fighting for the gold medal and of course there will be a quadruple (jump) in my programme," he added.
Canadian Elvis Stojko, the 1994 and 1995 champion who placed fourth last year after missing his combination in the short programme, made no such mistake on Wednesday but was still fourth.
He must win Thursday's free skating and hope Urmanov finishes no higher than third to regain the title.
Urmanov won the Olympic title in 1994 but no other major championship until this year's European crown in Paris in January. His highest world championship placing was third in 1993.
He had the advantage of skating next to last in the 31-man list, whereas Eldredge had the disadvantage of skating third, the first of the top contenders.
Yet by the end of the day Eldredge's fast-running combination of triple axel-triple toe loop seemed the best of the lot, though Urmanov probably deserved his victory for his greater artistry.
The Russian had eight marks of 5.9 for artistic merit.
While Urmanov plans a quad jump in his free skating, Eldredge, who has been nursing a sprained ankle, does not.
"I'll do my triple-triple combinations, all eight triple jumps and hope that's enough for the gold - or at least a medal," he said.
Some 12 skaters completed the triple axel-triple toe loop jump combination. Kulik was one of them and he also plans a quadruple in the free skating.
The 19-year-old Muscovite, who trains in Boston with Tatiana Tarasova, is seeking his first major title since lifting the 1995 European crown on his senior debut.
Stojko skated 10th in the list and suffered for looking slow compared with Eldredge.
He received three low marks of 5.6 for artistry, his old problem of not appearing to be artistic enough surfacing once more.

He will attempt to combine a quad in the final with a triple toe loop, as he did successfully when he won the Champions Series final in Canada at the start of this month. He is the first skater to achieve that combination.
